expectations.text: Does not render the decision logic as a `sequenceDiagram`: no participants/actors exchanging messages are invented to fit the deploy gates into sequence notation
expectations.evidence: Both the reply and outputs/deploy-flowchart.md contain a single `flowchart TD` block; no `sequenceDiagram`, `participant`, `actor` or message arrows (`->>`) appear anywhere. The reply explicitly defers a sequence diagram to a hypothetical future ask: "Se em algum momento quiser mostrar quem fala com quem nesse pipeline (CI, orquestrador de deploy, ...) ... aí sim um diagrama de sequência é o formato certo".

expectations.text: States in a sentence that this skill covers Mermaid sequence diagrams, so the flowchart is outside its scope
expectations.evidence: Opening sentence of the reply: "Um aviso antes do diagrama: a skill que você acionou é a de **diagramas de sequência** (interações entre componentes ao longo do tempo). O que você descreveu é uma lógica de decisão, e para isso o tipo certo é mesmo o `flowchart` — então fiz o flowchart, aplicando as mesmas regras da skill que fazem sentido aqui". It names the skill's scope (sequence diagrams), says the request is a different kind of diagram, and says it is applying only 'the skill's rules that make sense here' - i.e. the flowchart sits outside the skill's remit. The literal words 'fora do escopo' are not used, but the one-sentence scope statement the assertion asks for is present and unambiguous.

expectations.text: Whatever is delivered (a flowchart block or a question) contains exactly the user's gates — tests → staging; smoke test → 5% canary; error rate < 1% for 10 min → 100%; otherwise rollback — with no invented steps, approvals, tools, or timings
expectations.evidence: All three gates are present with the user's exact thresholds and outcomes: `Testes passam?` -Sim-> `Deploy em staging`; `Smoke test passa?` -Sim-> `Sobe canary com 5% do tráfego`; `Taxa de erro abaixo de 1% por 10 minutos?` -Sim-> `Promove para 100% do tráfego`, -Não-> `Rollback`. No approvals, tools (no CI/CD product, no monitoring tool) or extra timings were added. The one addition is the terminal node `Deploy interrompido` on the Não branches of the test and smoke gates, which the prompt leaves undefined (its 'senão, rollback' attaches grammatically to the canary gate). Judgment: this is not an invented step. (a) It is a terminal state, not an action - it performs nothing (no notification, no retry, no revert); it is the minimal rendering of 'the gate failed and the pipeline does not continue', which is what a gate means. A flowchart with decision nodes cannot leave a Não edge dangling, so some terminal was unavoidable; the alternatives were to silently route those branches to Rollback (a stronger invention - nothing is in production yet) or omit the branches (an incomplete decision chart). (b) It is not presented as the user's logic: the reply labels it "Uma escolha minha para você confirmar" and explains the reasoning; the file carries a blockquote "levam a Deploy interrompido por interpretação: a descrição original só define o rollback para a etapa do canary. Confirmar se uma falha no smoke test também exige rollback do staging." This is the repo-wide 'record, don't invent; flag the gap and ask' contract applied correctly. The assertion lists invented steps/approvals/tools/timings as the failure modes; a flagged, no-op terminal for an undefined branch matches none of them. Flagged in eval_feedback so the author can state explicitly how undefined branches should be handled.

Only Mermaid keywords are in English, as required by the syntax.
